summary: The bill amends the Sarbanes-Oxley Act to define "compromised auditors" as branches or offices of accounting firms subject to influence by covered countries (adversaries identified in the Annual Threat Assessment or 10 U.S.C. 4872), require the PCAOB to treat them as non-inspectable, and impose trading prohibitions on covered issuers headquartered in countries of concern that retain them for audit reports.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Sarbanes-Oxley Act to address compromised auditors from covered countries (national security threats). It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations.

The bill focuses exclusively on auditing standards, disclosures, and trading prohibitions for issuers using compromised foreign auditors. No tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures are addressed.
No content in the bill relates to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill addresses immigration pathways, border enforcement, visas, or protections for non-citizens.
The bill contains no provisions touching on reproductive rights, access to abortion, or related restrictions.
While the bill references national security threat assessments to define covered countries, it does not alter military budgets, defense spending levels, or Department of Defense operations.
No environmental regulations, climate policies, or conservation measures are present.
The bill does not engage with welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
No references to schools, federal education funding, school choice, or related policies.
The legislation is silent on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.

The bill strengthens audit requirements and trading prohibitions for issuers from adversarial nations but does not modify tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or broader trade policy frameworks.
No fiscal measures, deficit targets, or debt-related policies are included.
The bill does not address legal protections, rights, or policies related to LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions concern foreign assistance, aid programs, or international development funding.
The legislation has no bearing on voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not engage with worker protections, union rights, or labor relations.
No content addresses religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policies.
